What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 1

    Discover

    1–2 weeks

    We spend time at the front desk, on the gym floor, at the salon reception or with the coaching team to see how inquiries, bookings, renewals and check-ins really happen, and which systems hold the data. We confirm what the gym, salon or coaching software allows through APIs or exports, and choose the first journey to automate.

    Deliverables

    • Current member journey map with drop-off points
    • System and integration inventory, including access control and payment gateway
    • Prioritized automation shortlist with indicative effort
    • Baseline measures for the chosen journey

    What we need from you

    • Read access or exports from the gym, salon, studio or coaching software
    • Time with front-desk, trainer, stylist or coach leads
    • Current price list and membership, freeze, refund and cancellation policies
    • WhatsApp Business account and Meta business verification status
  2. 2

    Design

    1–2 weeks

    We design booking, reminder, follow-up and renewal flows, intake and check-in forms, routing rules and approval points, and write templates for WhatsApp, DLT SMS and email. Consent wording, health declarations, photo handling and retention are designed with the client's compliance owner, and a head trainer or lead dietitian sets the concern and referral rules.

    Deliverables

    • Flow diagrams with human checkpoints marked
    • Template drafts for WhatsApp, DLT SMS and email approval
    • Data map for consent, health data, photos, retention and access
    • Concern and referral rules for trainers, teachers and coaches
    • Acceptance criteria and test scenarios

    What we need from you

    • Brand voice and approved facts, prices and policies
    • Consent and privacy notice wording reviewed by the client's legal or compliance owner
    • Sign-off on health screening and referral rules from a qualified professional
    • Decisions on freeze, no-show, deposit and discount limits
  3. 3

    Build

    2–6 weeks

    We build the workflows in n8n or code, the secure forms and staff dashboards, AI prompts grounded in approved content, and the connections to the client's booking, access and payment systems, all in a staging setup with test data.

    Deliverables

    • Working workflows and integrations in staging
    • Secure intake, readiness and check-in forms
    • Staff dashboards for trainers, stylists and coaches
    • AI prompts with evaluation sets and refusal rules
    • Monitoring, alerts and error handling

    What we need from you

    • API credentials or vendor support for a test environment
    • Sample anonymized member and booking data
    • Feedback from trainers, stylists or coaches on the staff dashboards
  4. 4

    Validate & launch

    1–2 weeks

    Staff test real scenarios: a full class with a waitlist, a color client with no patch test on record, a failed UPI Autopay debit, a freeze request outside policy and a check-in that mentions dizziness. We test AI drafts against an evaluation set, launch at one location or with one coaching team first, and train every shift.

    Deliverables

    • Test results against acceptance criteria
    • AI draft evaluation report
    • Shift-wise training and quick reference guides
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan

    What we need from you

    • Staff time for scenario testing and training
    • Sign-off from the owner and the compliance owner
    • Approved templates live in the WhatsApp Business account and on DLT
  5. 5

    Operate & improve

    Ongoing, reviewed monthly

    We monitor workflow health, response times, renewal and no-show measures and AI quality, fix failures, and review results with the owner each month. New locations, services, programs and templates are added through the same approval process.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly performance and exception review
    • Workflow health and failure alerts
    • Template, rule and prompt change log
    • Roadmap for the next journey or location

    What we need from you

    • A named owner for decisions at each location
    • Feedback from staff, members and clients
    • Notice of changes to prices, policies, staff or software

First pilot: One location or coaching team, one journey, four to six weeks

We start where leakage is clearest. For a gym or studio that is usually trial booking and follow-up plus attendance-drop alerts at one location. For a salon it is booking, reminders and rebooking at one outlet, and for a coaching business, intake routing and weekly check-ins for one team. A baseline taken in the first week keeps the comparison honest.

  • One location, outlet or coaching team and one member journey
  • Approved WhatsApp templates and secure forms
  • Integration with the gym, salon or coaching software in read and limited write mode
  • A staff dashboard with escalation to a named manager
  • Weekly check-ins and a go or no-go review at the end of the pilot

Ways to work together

Choose the engagement that fits your stage.

  • Pilot sprint

    One automation, one segment and one accountable owner. We build, validate and measure it against agreed acceptance criteria before anything wider is committed.

    Best for: Proving value and fit with low risk

  • Phased rollout

    A prioritized roadmap across the journey, released in reviewed increments, with training and documentation after each release.

    Best for: Teams ready to connect several workflows

  • Operate & improve

    Monthly reviews of measures and exceptions, template and rule updates, and new automations as priorities change, during business hours.

    Best for: Keeping automations accurate as the business changes

Safe by design, owned by your team

  • Consent is recorded per person and channel; service, marketing and optional items such as progress photos have separate consent, and an opt-out on any channel applies across WhatsApp, SMS and email.
  • Health declarations, measurements, photos and food logs are visible only to the people who need them, never enter marketing tools or ad audiences, and are deleted on an agreed schedule.
  • Trainers, teachers and coaches do not diagnose; nutrition plans are written by qualified professionals, and injuries, health concerns and warning signs go to a person and, where needed, to the client's doctor.
  • AI drafts, summarizes and classifies from approved content; prices, discounts, refunds, freezes outside policy, public replies and plan changes always need a named person's approval.
  • Marketing avoids unsupported weight-loss, inch-loss and beauty claims and unverified before-and-after images, and influencer posts carry an upfront disclosure label.
  • Templates, rules and prompts are versioned and approved before going live, failures raise alerts, AI quality is sampled monthly, and access is reviewed quarterly and whenever staff leave.

The obligations that shape the design

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

  • Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025

    Contact details, attendance, measurements, progress photos, health declarations and food logs are personal data. The Rules notified on 13 November 2025 phase in itemized notice, consent as easy to withdraw as to give, security safeguards, breach intimation and erasure, mostly from May 2027; MeitY has consulted on bringing dates forward. Members under eighteen need verifiable parental consent, and tracking or targeted ads aimed at children are barred.

    meity.gov.in · Source

  • ASCI Code, influencer guidelines and health and wellness endorsements

    ASCI requires objective claims to be truthful and substantiated, and its complaints council has upheld complaints against slimming center ads with unsupported inch-loss and weight-loss figures and before-and-after images. Influencer posts need an upfront label such as Ad or Collaboration, and creators giving health or nutrition advice must hold and disclose relevant qualifications. Consumer Affairs guidance on health endorsements adds disclaimers.

    ascionline.in · Source

  • Auto-renewals: RBI e-mandate framework and dark patterns guidelines

    Recurring card, UPI and prepaid debits run on e-mandates under RBI's framework: registration with additional authentication, a notice at least 24 hours before each debit, the option to skip a debit or cancel the mandate, and extra authentication above ₹15,000. The consumer authority's 2023 dark patterns guidelines name subscription traps, such as hidden or cumbersome cancellation, so renewal flows state the price, date and an easy way to cancel.

    rbi.org.in · Source

  • WhatsApp Business Messaging and Commerce policies

    Businesses may message only people who opted in, must use approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window, must honor opt-outs and must offer a clear path to a person when automating. WhatsApp's commerce rules also restrict unsafe ingestible supplements and diet or weight-loss content that plays on negative self-perception, so fitness and nutrition messages stay factual and respectful.

    business.whatsapp.com · Source

  • TRAI TCCCPR rules for SMS and calls

    Commercial SMS and calls in India use DLT-registered headers and templates and must respect registered preferences. The 2025 amendment added -P, -S, -T and -G header suffixes, an opt-out in promotional messages and a 90-day wait before asking again after an opt-out. TRAI amended the consent provisions again in September 2026, so consent records and templates are checked against the current text.

    trai.gov.in · Source

  • Google review policy and India's online review standard

    Google's Maps policy bars paying or rewarding people for reviews, discouraging negative reviews and selectively asking happy customers. India's voluntary IS 19000:2022 standard on online consumer reviews sets similar principles for genuine, unbiased reviews. Our flows invite every client the same way and avoid staff review quotas, scripted requests to name staff and pressure to review at the counter.

    support.google.com · Source

Frequently asked

Do we need to change our gym, salon or coaching software?

No. We connect to the systems you already use through their APIs, integration options or scheduled exports. Where a system allows only limited access, we design around it, for example by preparing a list for staff to act on instead of writing into the software directly. Naming a product on this page does not imply a partnership with its vendor.

Can we send WhatsApp messages to all our members?

Only to people who shared their number and agreed to hear from you. Outside the 24-hour window after a member's last message, WhatsApp allows only approved templates, priced per delivered message by category. We help you capture opt-in at joining, write templates in the right categories, and fall back to email or DLT-registered SMS for members who have not opted in.

Will AI give our members diet or workout advice?

No. AI drafts messages, summarizes check-ins and formats plans that qualified people have written. Exercise programs come from your trainers, nutrition plans from qualified dietitians or nutritionists, and anything that sounds medical is routed to a person and, where needed, to the member's own doctor.

How do you handle progress photos, measurements and health forms?

They are optional wherever possible, collected through secure forms on your domain with clear consent, stored separately with restricted access, never used in marketing without separate written permission, and deleted on a schedule you approve. India's DPDP Act and Rules shape this design, and the same approach supports GDPR, which treats health data as a special category.

Can we auto-renew memberships and retry failed payments?

Yes, within the rules. Recurring debits run on UPI Autopay or card mandates through your payment gateway, where the bank sends the pre-debit notice and handles authentication. We make the renewal date, price and cancellation route clear in advance, retry only as the mandate allows, and have staff call members after repeated failures rather than blocking access automatically.

Can we reward members or staff for Google reviews?

No. Google's policy bars incentives for reviews, discouraging negative reviews and asking only happy customers. We also avoid staff review quotas and scripts asking customers to name staff, invite every client the same way, keep referral rewards separate from reviews, and have managers approve every public reply.

Does the GST change affect invoices and commission reports?

Since 22 September 2025, beauty and physical well-being services in India, including gyms, salons, spas and yoga, carry 5% GST without input tax credit, though yoga offered as a charitable activity by a registered trust may be exempt. We read tax amounts from your billing software rather than recalculating them, and commission statements use values net of GST. Your accountant confirms the treatment for your services.

We also coach clients abroad. Does this work for them?

Yes. Notices, consent records and deletion rules are set up so your adviser can check them against GDPR for EU and UK clients, where health data needs explicit consent or another specific legal condition. In the US, HIPAA usually applies only to covered health care providers and those working for them, while health and fitness apps outside HIPAA can fall under the FTC's Health Breach Notification Rule.
